compatibility.title: Which Subaru Models Use the EJ257?

failures.title: Subaru EJ257 Engine Problems - What Actually Fails
failures.goodYearsLine: Post-2008 EJ257 units received dual AVCS (variable intake and exhaust valve timing), raised compression from 8.0:1 to 8.2:1, and power increased to 300 hp. The later engines are more refined but share the same fundamental vulnerabilities. The best EJ257 to buy is one with documented head gasket replacement (MLS) and timing belt service already completed .

variants.title: EJ257 Variants - Which One Is in Your Car?
variants.intro: INTRO: While the EJ257 is a single engine code, there are distinct revisions across the production run. The differences matter - particularly when buying a replacement, as not all EJ257 variants are direct swaps. ### EJ257 - 2005-2007 (GD Impreza WRX STI) - Fitted to: Subaru GD Impreza WRX STI (2005-2007) - Key technical difference: 2.5-litre turbo petrol F4, 6-speed manual. Single AVCS (variable intake valve timing only). Compression ratio: 8.0:1. Power: 206 kW (280 hp) at 5,600 rpm, 392 Nm at 4,000 rpm. VF39 turbocharger. - Sub-code-specific failure note: Shares the family head gasket, ringland, and timing belt patterns. Early EJ257s are the most prone to ringland failure. - Interchange note: Direct swap with later EJ257 variants requires ECU reflash and may need different turbo plumbing. ### EJ257 - 2008-2014 (GE/GH Impreza WRX STI) - Fitted to: Subaru GE/GH Impreza WRX STI (2008-2014) - Key technical difference: Dual AVCS (variable intake and exhaust valve timing). Compression ratio raised to 8.2:1. Power: 221 kW (300 hp) at 6,000 rpm, 407 Nm at 4,000 rpm. VF48 turbocharger (larger than the earlier VF39). - Sub-code-specific failure note: Shares the family patterns. The VF48 turbo is more durable than the VF39 but still suffers oil starvation if maintenance is poor. The higher compression and power output place additional stress on head gaskets and ringlands. - Interchange note: Not a straight swap with earlier EJ257s - ECU, turbo, and wiring loom differ significantly. ### EJ257 - 2014-2021 (VA WRX STI) - Fitted to: Subaru VA WRX STI (2014-2021) - Key technical difference: Dual AVCS. Power: 221 kW (300 hp) at 6,000 rpm, 407 Nm at 4,000 rpm. Revised ECU calibration and improved cooling. Last variant of the EJ engine family. - Sub-code-specific failure note: The later EJ257s are more refined but share the same fundamental vulnerabilities. Ringland failure remains a concern on modified cars. - Interchange note: Not a straight swap with earlier EJ257s without full ECU, loom, and ancillaries.

buyingGuide.title: Buying a Replacement EJ257 - What to Choose

options.label: Used
options.body: A used EJ257 makes sense only if it comes with documented evidence of head gasket replacement (MLS units), a recent timing belt service, and a compression test showing healthy cylinder pressures. Without this documentation, a used EJ257 is a very high-risk purchase - ringland failure and head gasket failure are common, and many have been modified and abused. Given the EJ257 is an interference engine, any used unit without timing belt history is a gamble.

options.label: Reconditioned
options.body: A proper EJ257 recon addresses the known weak points: new MLS head gaskets (not factory-spec), new timing belt kit with tensioner and idlers, new water pump, new turbocharger oil feed lines, and a thorough inspection of the turbocharger (VF39/VF48). Reconditioned units typically include a 12-month warranty and are the sweet spot for most UK owners - you get the reliability upgrades without the cost of a full rebuild.

options.label: Rebuilt
options.body: A full EJ257 rebuild is justified when you want to keep a specific car (e.g. a clean STI with low body mileage) and want the engine to last another 100,000+ miles. An upgraded rebuild should include forged pistons (the factory cast pistons are a weak point), ARP head studs, a fully reconditioned turbocharger, a new oil pump, and often upgraded bearings. Budget £4,000-£6,000 for a quality rebuild with forged internals.

buyingGuide.supplyFitLine: All of our vetted UK Subaru specialists offer supply-only or full supply-and-fit - nationwide delivery and recovery available, with warranties that cover both parts and labour.
buyingGuide.vehicleValueNote: The EJ257 sits exclusively in WRX STI models - values range from £8,000-£20,000 for the GD/GE/GH generations, £15,000-£35,000 for the VA generation, depending on condition and mileage. A reconditioned EJ257 at £2,500-£4,500 represents 15-50% of vehicle value - generally viable for most examples. However, for a high-mileage (£8,000-£10,000) GD STI, a full rebuild at £4,000-£6,000 may approach 50-60% of the vehicle's value. In those cases, evaluate the car's overall condition, rust, and interior before committing. A clean, low-mileage STI justifies the spend; a tired one may be better broken for parts .

items.question: How much does a Subaru EJ257 engine replacement cost?
items.answer: A reconditioned EJ257 supply-only costs £2,500-£4,500, with fitted prices from £3,500-£5,700. Used units start from £2,000 supply-only. Rebuilt engines with forged internals cost £4,000-£6,000 supply-only.
bullets: Rebuilt engines with forged internals cost £4,000-£6,000 supply‑only.

items.question: What are the most common EJ257 engine problems?
items.answer: The EJ257 suffers from head gasket failure (70k-120k miles), piston ringland failure (especially on modified cars), timing belt failure if the 100,000 km / 5-year service is missed, and turbocharger wear on the VF39/VF48 units. Head gasket replacement with MLS gaskets costs £1,200-£2,500. Forged piston rebuild costs £2,500-£4,500. Preventative timing belt service £500-£900.
bullets: Head gasket replacement with MLS gaskets costs £1,200-£2,500.

items.question: Which Subaru models use the EJ257 engine?
items.answer: The EJ257 was fitted exclusively to the Subaru Impreza WRX STI (GD: 2005-2007; GE/GH: 2008-2014) and the Subaru WRX STI (VA: 2014-2021). The GD generation uses a VF39 turbo; the GE/GH and VA generations use a VF48 turbo.
bullets: The GD generation uses a VF39 turbo.
The GE/GH and VA generations use a VF48 turbo.

items.question: Should I buy a used or reconditioned EJ257?
items.answer: A reconditioned EJ257 is the safer choice - it includes new MLS head gaskets, a full timing kit, and a 12-month warranty. Used units are only recommended with documented head gasket and timing belt history, plus a compression test. A used EJ257 without history is a very high-risk purchase.
bullets: Used units are only recommended with documented head gasket and timing belt history, plus a compression test.
A used EJ257 without history is a very high‑risk purchase.

items.question: What’s the difference between EJ257 and EJ255?
items.answer: The EJ257 is the STI‑spec engine with stronger internals (semi‑closed deck block, different pistons, larger VF39/VF48 turbo) and 280-300 hp. The EJ255 is the WRX‑spec engine with a smaller TD04 turbo, open‑deck block, and 227-265 hp. See the EJ255 page for details
bullets: The EJ257 is more powerful and more expensive to replace.
They are not directly interchangeable without ECU and wiring changes.

items.question: How long does an EJ257 engine last?
items.answer: With regular maintenance (timing belt every 100,000 km / 5 years, oil changes every 5k miles), an EJ257 can exceed 150,000 miles. Ringland failure is the main limit on modified or poorly maintained cars. Head gasket failure often occurs around 80k-120k miles unless upgraded.
bullets: Ringland failure is the main limit on modified or poorly maintained cars.
Head gasket failure often occurs around 80k-120k miles unless upgraded.
